parts.text: Describe how yoghurt is made.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to four of the following:
• milk is sterilised / pasteurised (1)
• cooled to about 40 °C (1)
• Lactobacillus added (1)
• incubated for several hours (1)
• lactose converted to lactic acid / pH falls and milk thickens (1)

parts.text: Describe how yeast is used to make bread.

• yeast mixed with flour, water and sugar (1)
• dough left in a warm place (1)
• yeast respires anaerobically / ferments sugar (1)
• carbon dioxide makes dough rise (1)
• ethanol evaporates during baking (1)

parts.text: Describe the methods used to farm large numbers of fish.

• maintain water quality / oxygen / remove waste (1)
• separate fish by size or species to control predation (1)
• control disease with antibiotics / vaccination / pesticides for lice (1)
• control quality and frequency of feeding (1)
• selective breeding for fast growth (1)

• sterile / filtered air supply (1)
• sealed so no microorganisms enter (1)

parts.text: Describe how you could investigate the effect of temperature on anaerobic respiration in yeast.

intro: A grower wanted to find out whether adding carbon dioxide to a glasshouse would increase the yield of lettuces.

parts.text:
Design an investigation to find out the effect of carbon dioxide concentration on the growth of lettuces in a glasshouse.

Include experimental details in your answer and write in full sentences.

rows.answer:
An answer that makes reference to six of the following:
• C – change the carbon dioxide concentration (at least five values / a suitable range) (1)
• O – use lettuces of the same variety and age (1)
• R – repeat each test at least three times and calculate a mean (1)
• M1 – measure the mass of lettuces harvested (1)
• M2 – measure over the same period of time / at the same time (1)
• S1 – control temperature (1)
• S2 – control light intensity (1)
• S – control water and fertiliser (1)
rows.notes: Allow S marks for any two other relevant control variables; credit a correctly described control experiment in place of one S mark

• plant the same number of lettuces in each (1)

• then levels off / stays constant from about 150 kg per hectare (1)
• uses data, e.g. 3.8 tonnes per hectare at 0 kg per hectare and 8.2 tonnes per hectare at 250 kg per hectare (1)
• rate of increase slows down (1)

• for growth (1)

intro: The diagram shows an industrial fermenter.

parts.text: Explain why conditions inside an industrial fermenter used to grow a fungus that makes penicillin are carefully controlled.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• aseptic conditions: sterilised with steam (1)
• prevents contamination by other microorganisms (1)
• nutrients supply energy / raw materials for growth (1)
• optimum temperature for enzymes (1)
• water jacket removes heat from respiration (1)
• optimum pH monitored with a probe (1)
• oxygen supplied for aerobic respiration (1)
• stirring mixes contents evenly (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

parts.text: Explain the role of yeast in making bread.

rows.answer:
An explanation that makes reference to six of the following:
• yeast respires anaerobically (1)
• glucose → ethanol + carbon dioxide (1)
• enzymes in yeast / flour break down starch to sugar (1)
• carbon dioxide bubbles make dough rise / beer fizzy (1)
• warm temperature for enzyme activity (1)
• baking kills yeast (1)
• ethanol evaporates during baking (1)
• ethanol remains in beer (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

parts.text: Describe how yoghurt is made using bacteria.

rows.answer:
A description that makes reference to six of the following:
• milk is pasteurised / heated to kill microorganisms (1)
• cooled to about 40 °C (1)
• Lactobacillus bacteria added (1)
• incubated at a warm temperature (1)
• bacteria ferment lactose (1)
• lactic acid produced (1)
• pH falls so milk proteins coagulate / thicken (1)
• cooled to stop the process; acid stops harmful bacteria (1)
rows.notes: max 6. Credit any other valid biological points.

• sticky ends join (1)

• recombinant plasmid is a vector (1)

• bacteria grown in a fermenter (1)

parts.text: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of growing genetically modified crops.

rows.answer:
A discussion that makes reference to six of the following:
• higher yield / more food (1)
• resistant to pests so less pesticide used (1)
• herbicide resistance makes weed control easier (1)
• can grow in drought / poor soil (1)
• improved nutrition, e.g. extra vitamin (1)
• genes may spread to wild plants (1)
• effects on food chains / insects (1)
• seeds can be expensive / ethical concerns (1)
rows.notes: max 6. At least one advantage and one disadvantage are needed for full marks.

parts.text: Compare selective breeding and genetic modification as ways of producing better crop plants.

rows.answer:

• genetic modification transfers genes directly (1)
• GM can use genes from another species / transgenic (1)
• GM is faster (1)
• selective breeding takes many generations (1)
• both produce organisms with useful features (1)
• both can reduce genetic variation (1)
• GM needs restriction enzymes, ligase and vectors (1)
